record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Develop better methods for computing open-loop periodic solutions for hybrid biped models when those solutions must be combined with virtual constraints and, ideally, also satisfy energy-efficiency objectives. The challenge is to avoid the difficulty caused by numerous local minima and to obtain periodic solutions suitable for feedback-law design.

evidence.quote: Our experience is that finding periodic solutions in this manner is difficult due to numerous local minima. The problem is even more difficult when seeking solutions that are energy efficient, in addition to being periodic.
Other approaches to finding periodic orbits, such as those in Srinivasan and Ruina [2006] and Posa et al. [2014], need to be considered when designing feedback laws through virtual constraints.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hybrid dynamical model of a 3D bipedal walker, consisting of (i) continuous-time Lagrangian dynamics during single-support phases of the form $D(q)\ddot q + C(q,\dot q)\dot q + G(q) = B(q)u$, where $q\in Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ are generalized coordinates and $u\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is the control input, together with (ii) a discrete impact map $(q^+,\dot q^+) = \Delta(q^-,\dot q^-)$ that resets the state when a swing-foot guard surface $S=\{(q,\dot q): h(q)=0,\, L_{\dot q}h(q)<0\}$ is reached. A solution $(q(\cdot),\dot q(\cdot),u(\cdot))$ is called a hybrid periodic orbit of period $T>0$ if it satisfies the continuous dynamics on $[0,T)$, hits $S$ at $t=T^-$, and $(q(0),\dot q(0)) = \Delta(q(T^-),\dot q(T^-))$.

A virtual-constraint controller is specified by a smooth output $y = h_c(q) - h_d(\theta(q))$, where $\theta:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ is a monotonic phasing variable and $h_d$ is a parametrized desired profile (e.g., Bézier polynomials with parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^N$). The zero dynamics manifold $Z_\alpha = \{(q,\dot q): y=0,\,\dot y=0\}$ is required to be invariant under both the continuous dynamics (under the feedback that zeros $y$) and the impact map.

Problem. Develop a numerical method that, given the hybrid model and a class of virtual constraints parametrized by $\alpha$, computes an open-loop periodic state-input trajectory $(q^*(\cdot),\dot q^*(\cdot),u^*(\cdot))$ together with parameters $\alpha^*$ such that:
(a) the trajectory is a hybrid periodic orbit of the closed-loop system with $y\equiv 0$ on the orbit (i.e., the orbit lies in $Z_{\alpha^*}$ and is invariant under $\Delta$),
(b) the cost functional $J(\alpha) = \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T \|u^*(t)\|^2\,dt$ (or another energy-efficiency criterion such as cost of transport) is minimized, subject to inequality constraints encoding ground-reaction feasibility, friction-cone, joint-limit, and unilateral-contact conditions,
(c) the method overcomes the proliferation of spurious local minima that plague direct nonlinear-programming formulations of this combined periodicity-plus-efficiency problem, and
(d) the resulting periodic solution and parameters $\alpha^*$ are directly usable for designing exponentially stabilizing feedback laws via hybrid zero dynamics.

Provide such an algorithm (or prove an obstruction) that reliably produces certified periodic, energy-efficient solutions for 3D biped models with $n\geq 7$ degrees of freedom.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of jointly computing energy-efficient periodic gaits compatible with virtual constraints for 3D hybrid bipeds remains an active research area. Subsequent work (e.g., FROST by Hereid–Ames, direct collocation with hybrid zero dynamics, and contact-implicit trajectory optimization extensions of Posa et al.) has produced improved tools but no method is universally accepted as resolving the local-minima difficulty for high-DOF 3D bipeds with simultaneous efficiency objectives. The problem is best classified as still open / partially advanced.

status_evidence.title: FROST: Fast Robot Optimization and Simulation Toolkit
status_evidence.snippet: Hereid and Ames present a direct-collocation toolkit tailored to hybrid systems with virtual constraints, addressing periodic gait generation for bipeds.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made on optimization frameworks for hybrid periodic gaits with virtual constraints, but local-minima issues persist.

status_evidence.title: Posa, Cantu, Tedrake — Direct method for trajectory optimization through contact
status_evidence.snippet: Contact-implicit trajectory optimization for systems with impacts.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative methods exist but are not specifically tailored to virtual-constraint feedback design.
